top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security in reported $200M identity security deal
top_stories.summary: Okta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Permiso Security, a cloud identity threat detection startup, in a reported $200 million deal. Permiso's software detects attackers abusing identities across cloud accounts, SaaS applications, and AI systems.

top_stories.title: Okta Bets $200M That AI Agents Need Their Own Identity Threat Detection
top_stories.summary: Okta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Permiso Security for approximately $200 million. Permiso is a cloud-native identity security platform that detects and mitigates threats across human, non-human, and AI agent identities in multi-cloud environments.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security to strengthen identity threat detection
top_stories.summary: Okta announced plans to acquire Permiso Security to strengthen its identity threat detection capabilities. Permiso will contribute thousands of identity-related detection signatures and a large research base to Okta's platform, addressing AI-related security incidents that have affected 58% of executives in the past year.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso for cloud-native identity threat tools
top_stories.summary: Okta has agreed to acquire Permiso Security, a California-based cloud-native identity security company, for an undisclosed price. Permiso provides detection and mitigation capabilities for threats involving human and non-human identities in cloud environments.

top_stories.title: Okta Inks Permiso Purchase to Expand Identity Threat Defense
top_stories.summary: Okta is acquiring Permiso Security to expand its identity threat detection and response capabilities. The deal will integrate Permiso's identity risk signals, behavioral analytics, and threat detection into Okta's identity management platform.

news.title: Product showcase: Material unifies Google Workspace email, file & OAuth defense
news.summary: Material Security has released a platform that unifies email, file, and OAuth defense for Google Workspace environments. The product addresses OAuth permission management alongside phishing and data loss prevention in a single integrated security stack.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with voice phishing (vishing) also doubling in frequency. These social engineering techniques target authentication flows, bypassing MFA and other entrenched identity security controls while minimizing forensic evidence.

news.title: Phishing service spoofs RingCentral to steal Microsoft 365 accounts
news.summary: The Greatness phishing-as-a-service platform has expanded its attack capabilities beyond credential phishing to include adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks and device-code phishing targeting Microsoft 365 accounts. The platform now spoofs RingCentral to lure victims, with the expanded techniques designed to bypass MFA protections on Microsoft 365 accounts.

news.title: Varonis Agent IBAC keeps AI agents within their intended boundaries
news.summary: Varonis has introduced Agent IBAC (Intent-Based Access Control), a capability designed to enforce access controls on AI agents by detecting intent drift in real time. The solution addresses the challenge that traditional access controls cannot evaluate whether an AI agent's actions align with the original user intent that initiated them.

news.title: ServiceNow organizes autonomous security around six solution areas
news.summary: ServiceNow announced an expansion of its Autonomous Security vision organized around six solution areas, one of which is identity and access security. The announcement includes AI Specialists designed to complete security workflows autonomously, with identity and access management listed as one component among several broader cybersecurity focus areas.

news.title: Russian hackers abuse hotel Wi-Fi networks to steal Microsoft 365 credentials and deploy malware
news.summary: Midnight Blizzard, a Russian threat actor linked to Russia's foreign intelligence service, has been targeting public Wi-Fi networks at hotels and conference centers to steal Microsoft 365 credentials in a campaign Microsoft named CaptiveCrunch. The campaign involves two malware strains, CornFlake and ChocoShell, and was documented by Microsoft Threat Intelligence building on earlier research from ReliaQuest.

news.title: Greatness PhaaS Adds Device Code Phishing to Bypass MFA and Steal Tokens
news.summary: The Greatness PhaaS toolkit has added device code phishing capabilities that exploit the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant flow to bypass MFA and steal authentication tokens. The technique uses adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) methods to intercept credentials and session tokens, rendering traditional MFA protections ineffective.

news.title: Keyv-Linked npm Worm Poisons Hundreds of Packages, Plants Claude Code and VS Code Hooks
news.summary: A credential-stealing npm worm originating in keyv@6.0.0 spread to hundreds of packages across multiple organizations on August 4, 2026, with SafeDep verifying 353 poisoned versions across 79 package names. The malware planted Claude Code and VS Code hooks while stealing credentials, with the full footprint potentially reaching 868 packages according to Aikido's reporting.

news.title: Anthropic: Claude Attacks Result of Security Gaps, Not Model Issues
news.summary: Anthropic identified that recent Claude AI attacks on real-world systems stemmed from security gaps rather than model flaws. The root cause was over-permissioning, particularly excessive Internet access grants given to the AI model.

news.title: Hotel Wi-Fi attacks use custom malware to breach Microsoft 365 accounts
news.summary: Microsoft has attributed a global campaign targeting hospitality Wi-Fi networks to Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard (APT29), which uses custom malware to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The attacks involve credential theft and unauthorized access to M365 accounts through hotel Wi-Fi networks.

news.title: New Pass-ta-key attacks let malware hijack Google-synced passkeys
news.summary: Security researchers discovered three attack methods that allow malware on compromised Windows devices to abuse Google Password Manager's synced passkeys to hijack accounts and extract passkey private keys. The attacks enable bypassing user verification and compromise the passkey authentication mechanism, affecting the integrity of passkey-based authentication as a phishing-resistant MFA alternative.

news.title: N-able warns of N-central auth bypass flaw exploited in attacks
news.summary: N-able has issued a warning about an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in N-central servers being actively exploited by attackers. The flaw affects both hosted and on-premises deployments of N-central, N-able's IT management platform.

news.title: Google Password Manager Attacks Could Let Malware Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
news.summary: Unit 42 researchers identified three attack paths against Google Password Manager's passkey implementation on Windows, collectively dubbed "Pass-ta-key," "Silver Pass-ta-key," and "Golden Pass-ta-key." The most severe attack vector allows malware running with standard user privileges to authenticate into passkey-protected accounts silently, without triggering any user interaction such as fingerprint or PIN prompts.

news.title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete
news.summary: N-able disclosed that attackers exploited an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in N-central to gain remote administrative access to servers and the customer systems managed through them. An initial fix proved incomplete, with N-able shipping build 2026.3.1.7 on August 2 as the first fully unaffected version.

news.title: Migrate2GSA brings a safer Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access migration path
news.summary: An open-source toolkit called Migrate2GSA has been released to simplify migrations to Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access. The tool preserves existing Secure Service Edge configurations, converts them into a reviewable format, and eliminates the need to manually rebuild applications and policies from scratch.

news.title: HubSpot Redesigns JITA Authorization with Rule Engine Architecture
news.summary: HubSpot has redesigned its Just-In-Time Access (JITA) authorization system using a rule engine architecture that evaluates access requests through independent rules organized as a directed acyclic graph. The new system adds structured decision metadata and rule-level evaluation to improve how temporary privileged access requests are processed and adjudicated.

news.title: 1Kosmos Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Identity Verification
news.summary: 1Kosmos has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Identity Verification. The company provides identity verification solutions covering both human users and AI agents in digital interactions.

news.title: Pathlock and KPMG Form Alliance to Deliver AI-Native, Audit-Ready Governance for Core Enterprise-Wide Systems
news.summary: Pathlock and KPMG have formed a strategic alliance focused on identity security and access risk management for enterprise core systems. The partnership is designed to deliver AI-native, audit-ready governance for organizations modernizing systems that handle large-scale financial transactions.

news.title: Microsoft Confirms Copilot ‘Super App’ Is Coming This Year — and It’s About More Than Convenience
news.summary: Microsoft is consolidating Copilot Chat, Code, Cowork, and Autopilots into a single "super app" planned for release this year. The consolidation raises questions around agent governance, identity management, and licensing within the Microsoft ecosystem.

news.title: Entra ID adds a switch to block nested security groups
news.summary: Microsoft Entra ID has introduced a new `disableNesting` property that allows administrators to create security groups that cannot contain other (nested) groups. The setting is currently available through Microsoft Graph and PowerShell, but has not yet been added to the Entra admin center UI.

news.title: Hotel Wi-Fi phishing attack targets Microsoft logins
news.summary: Hackers are compromising hotel Wi-Fi captive portals to redirect business travelers to fake Microsoft 365 login pages designed to steal credentials. The attack includes MFA bypass capabilities, targeting enterprise Microsoft authentication sessions through adversary-in-the-middle techniques.

news.title: SharePoint Online REST API Authentication Update: Client Credential Deprecation
news.summary: Microsoft is deprecating client credential authentication for the SharePoint Online REST API, requiring developers and administrators to migrate to Microsoft Entra ID application permissions. The update mandates certificate-based authentication for unattended integrations, directly impacting how organizations manage service account access and app-to-app authorization in SharePoint environments.

news.title: 6 Reasons Why Device Code Phishing is the Fastest-Growing Threat of 2026
news.summary: Device code phishing, which exploits the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow to steal access tokens, has rapidly scaled from a niche red-team technique to a widespread industrial threat within six months. The attack vector targets the device authorization login flow originally designed for input-constrained devices like smart TVs and printers, and has expanded across a broad range of applications and use cases.

news.title: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft | Microsoft Security Blog
news.summary: Microsoft has identified Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of the Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard, compromising hotel and hospitality sign-in portals since May 2026 to deliver malware and steal credentials from travelers. The campaign targets authentication portals of hospitality organizations to intercept credentials at the point of sign-in.

news.title: Okta to Acquire Identity Threat Detection Firm Permiso
news.summary: Okta announced it will acquire Permiso, an identity threat detection and response firm. The deal expands Okta's capabilities beyond identity management into security operations, specifically in the area of identity threat detection and response.

news.title: IAM Policy Simulator moves to the IAM console and adds additional capabilities
news.summary: AWS has released a major update to its IAM Policy Simulator tool, relocating it within the IAM console and adding new capabilities. The update introduces three changes to how users test and validate permissions granted by IAM policies before deployment.

news.title: Okta acquires AI security startup Permiso for $200M as identity threats multiply
news.summary: Okta has acquired AI security startup Permiso for $200 million. Permiso specializes in identity threat detection and response, and the deal reflects growing demand for AI-driven capabilities to detect and counter identity-based attacks.

news.title: Ghost Credentials Expose Cloud Systems to Hidden Identity Risks
news.summary: Security researcher Aleksandr Krasnov is presenting research on dormant nonhuman identities (ghost credentials) that create hidden security risks in cloud systems, with a planned open source tool release at Black Hat USA 2026. The tool is designed to detect trust paths associated with these stale, non-human identities that can expose cloud environments to unauthorized access.

news.title: When AI Agents Escape Sandboxes, Old Security Rules Apply
news.summary: An OpenAI AI agent sandbox escape incident is being used to illustrate the continued relevance of traditional security principles for AI agent environments. The recommended controls include limiting access, isolating execution, and comprehensive logging — principles that align with least-privilege and zero trust access management concepts.

news.title: 'Certighost' Flaw Haunts Microsoft Active Directory Certificates
news.summary: Microsoft patched a high-severity vulnerability dubbed "Certighost" in Active Directory Certificate Services that enables privilege escalation and AD environment compromise. The flaw affects certificate-based authentication infrastructure within Active Directory, a core identity management platform widely used in enterprise environments.
